research_question: In adults aged 50 years or older, what is the effect of the live attenuated Oka/Merck herpes zoster vaccine (Zostavax), compared with placebo, on the risk of experiencing one or more adverse events of any type during short-term post-vaccination safety follow-up?
treatment_label: Live attenuated Oka/Merck herpes zoster vaccine (Zostavax), any batch/dose, single administration
outcome_description: Number of participants reporting one or more adverse events of any type (injection-site or systemic, vaccine-related or not) during the short-term post-vaccination safety follow-up period as defined by each trial (e.g. days 0-28 or 0-42), out of the number randomised or vaccinated in each arm. Where adverse events were collected only in a designated safety substudy of a larger trial, the substudy event counts and denominators are used. Trials reporting multiple vaccine batches/doses are combined into a single vaccine group by summing events and participants. Percentages are converted to counts using the arm size to which they refer.
positive_direction: A risk ratio greater than 1 means that a larger proportion of participants experienced one or more adverse events in the live zoster vaccine group than in the placebo group (i.e. more adverse events, worse tolerability, with the vaccine).
search_queries: live attenuated zoster vaccine Zostavax randomised placebo-controlled trial adverse events safety
Oka/Merck varicella zoster vaccine older adults trial safety tolerability injection-site reactions
herpes zoster vaccine placebo controlled trial adults 50 years or older adverse event rates
inclusion_criteria: Randomised trial comparing the live attenuated Oka/Merck herpes zoster vaccine (Zostavax) with a placebo injection in adults, broadly including adults aged 50 years or older (mixed-age samples acceptable if mostly older adults)
Reports quantitative post-vaccination safety data, including the number of participants with one or more adverse events of any type (or percentages convertible to counts) with an arm denominator
Any publication year, language, country, or trial size; includes safety substudies nested within larger efficacy trials
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, pooled post-hoc summaries, editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, theoretical or modelling papers)

No comparison between a live zoster vaccine arm and a placebo arm (e.g. single-arm studies, observational surveillance, head-to-head comparisons of two vaccines, trials of the recombinant adjuvanted (non-live) zoster vaccine, or trials using a different vaccine or dosing schedule as comparator)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no events and totals, proportions, or convertible percentages for participants with one or more adverse events)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (not concerned with herpes zoster vaccination safety), or reports only efficacy against herpes zoster/post-herpetic neuralgia, immunogenicity, serious adverse events only, hospitalisations or death without any-adverse-event counts
moderators_to_extract: Mean or minimum age of enrolled participants (e.g. 50-59 vs 60+ vs 70+)
Length and definition of the safety follow-up window (e.g. 0-28 vs 0-42 days)
Method of adverse event ascertainment (diary card/report card vs investigator-reported)
Whether the data come from a dedicated safety substudy or the whole randomised trial
Vaccine potency/formulation (e.g. refrigerated vs frozen, PFU per dose) and number of doses combined
Sample size category and funding source (industry-sponsored vs independent)
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML, with Hartung-Knapp adjustment considered given few trials). Events = participants with ≥1 adverse event of any type; total = number randomised/vaccinated in each arm (prefer the randomised denominator even when the paper's percentages use a smaller complete-safety-data subset). Combine multiple vaccine batches/doses into one group; use safety-substudy counts and denominators when the outcome was only measured in the substudy. Heterogeneity assessed with I-squared and tau-squared; small-study effects not formally tested if fewer than 10 trials.
single_outcome_target: one or more adverse events (any adverse event)
